completed_units.question: Can the program detect, mechanically, that its own subject moved?

completed_units.evidence: Bitten against the real repository: an untracked core/_qm_freeze_probe.py gave exit 2; an appended newline in main.py gave exit 1; both together gave exit 3; main.py restored byte-identically (git hash-object 204c6a93 before and after); baseline exit 0 each time. Made durable in tests/test_qm_subject_freeze.py against a throwaway git repository, including the case that motivates it — a new module under core/ while `git diff --stat` against the snapshot stays empty.
completed_units.anti_vacuity: The one-operation ratchet was asked directly whether it governs the new file: in scope, one definition counted, six files governed. A guard nobody governs is the failure mode this program cannot afford.

completed_units.result: All eight CARRIED_FORWARD. Two map defects found, one code defect banked.

The widened stem index was probed (it resolves 'loop_memory_read') before its silence was trusted, and the sites for C00/C03 were recovered from their closure commits' test imports.

completed_units.protection_note: UNPROVEN deliberately. Nothing mechanically prevents a future production change from staling a carried-forward cluster silently; the carry-forward derivation is a script run by hand, not a guard in the suite. Whether that instrument should exist is a question for a later unit, not an assumption now.
